parole.significato: Deadjectival, denoting a carrier of the specified property (rare)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *-ъkъ via Old Church Slavonic -ъкъ (-ŭkŭ).

parole.significato: oriole (bird of genus Oriolus), particularly golden oriole (Oriolus oriolus)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *jьvьlga. Old Church Slavonic влъга (vlŭga).
From Proto-Slavic *blizьnьcь via Old Church Slavonic близньць (bliznĭcĭ). Doublet of standard близна́к (bliznák). Morphologically equivalent to бли́зо (blízo, “near”) + -нец (-nec).
Ultimately from Proto-Slavic *blędь: * For obsolete sense: Inherited from Old Church Slavonic блѧдь (blędĭ); * For derogatory sense: Borrowed from Russian блядь (bljadʹ).

parole.significato: malevolent female mythical creature, witch, ghost
parole.testo: Deverbal of Proto-Slavic *věděti (“to know, to wit”). Equivalent to Old Church Slavonic вѣдь (vědĭ, “knowledge”) + + -а (-a). Compare ве́щица (véštica), Russian ве́дьма (védʹma).
From Proto-Slavic *dǫbъ, via Old Church Slavonic дѫбъ (dǫbŭ).

parole.significato: bed for plants, garden plot (а raised shaped area of soil (such as a quadrangle, ellipse, etc.), convenient for plantin…
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *lě̄xà, whence also Old Church Slavonic лѣха (lěxa).

parole.significato: not to work, to rest, to take a break
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *počivati, an iterative of Old Church Slavonic почити (počiti) + -вам (-vam).

From Proto-Slavic *rьvьnivъ. Morphologically identical to ре́вен (réven, “zeal”) (dialectal) + -ив (-iv). The meaning jealous is probably inherited from Old Church Slavonic рьвьнивъ (rĭvĭnivŭ), while the dialectal desirable is native.
From Proto-Slavic *sьgъda. Attested as Old Church Slavonic сьга (sĭga), сєга (sega), сєгꙑ (segy) in Church Slavonic texts.
Etymologically from Proto-Slavic *ǫdolь. By surface analysis, юн- (jun-) + дол (dol, “dale”). Poetic meaning is inherited from Old Church Slavonic ѫдоль (ǫdolĭ).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ǫrodъ. By surface analysis, юн- (jun-) + род (rod, “birth, origin”). Poetic meaning is inherited from Old Church Slavonic ѫродъ (ǫrodŭ).
